elements.quote: Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023, to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.

elements.quote: Since the onset of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID19), SARS-CoV-2 infection has been circulating globally... The fact that SARS-CoV-2 is still mutating indicates that it remains a global health threat. The WHO study published in Nature [1, 3] also suggested that accurately tracking SARS-CoV-2 and its impact had been challenging.
elements.reason: The introduction describes the global circulation of SARS-CoV-2, the ongoing threat due to mutations, and the challenge of accurately tracking its impact, establishing the current state of knowledge and uncertainties.

elements.quote: In addition, the advantage of this study was that compared with the previous meta-analysis of the SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate, first, to avoid the heterogeneous impact of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection definition on SARSCoV-2 reinfection rates, so this study defined reinfection and included only literature with reinfection intervals greater than 90 days. Secondly, considering the heterogeneity of reinfection rates of different variants, we constructed a meta-regression of time-varying reinfection rates...
elements.reason: The authors explain the need for the review by highlighting limitations in previous meta-analyses (heterogeneity in definitions) and the specific methodological improvements (meta-regression of time-varying rates) they are introducing to address these gaps.

elements.quote: In addition, the advantage of this study was that compared with the previous meta-analysis of the SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate, first, to avoid the heterogeneous impact of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection definition on SARSCoV-2 reinfection rates, so this study defined reinfection and included only literature with reinfection intervals greater than 90 days.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly acknowledge the existence of previous meta-analyses and explain the need for the current review by contrasting their methodology (specifically regarding reinfection definitions) with those previous studies.
This is a systematic review of observational studies (reinfection rates), not a review of intervention effects; therefore, a mechanism of action is not applicable.
This is a systematic review of observational studies (reinfection rates), not a review of complex interventions or delivery contexts; therefore, a logic model is not applicable.

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to describe and summarize the current reinfection rates in different regions and among diverse populations. Furthermore, the study sought to examine trends in reinfection rates over time, so as to provide reference for the development of global unified reinfection standards and reinfection measures in the future.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the study's objectives, which are to describe and summarize current SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rates and to examine trends in these rates over time.
This review is an observational study of reinfection rates (prevalence/incidence), not a review of intervention effects; therefore, PICO comparisons are not applicable.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) Conformed to research questions, i.e., studies that estimated the reinfection rate of SARS-CoV-2 or we could calculate it based on the data provided in the paper; (2) The study design included cohort study, case-control study, and descriptive study; (3) The study fited our working definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection... The exclusion criteria were: (1) The sample size was less than 20; (2) Belonged to one of the following types of studies: editorial, case report, case series study, systematic review, meta-analysis, animal experiment, news report; (3) Secondary reporting or articles on repeated studies of the same population; (4) Grey literature
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists inclusion criteria (research question, study design, working definition) and exclusion criteria (sample size, study type, secondary reporting, grey literature).

elements.quote: To avoid language bias, the search was not limited to any language. We conducted preliminary screening based on the English title and English abstract provided by nonEnglish articles. Further, in the screening process, if the included article was neither in English nor in Chinese and did not provide an English abstract or full text, we used an online translator (Google Translate) for translation.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the criteria regarding language (no language limit, translation used).
The manuscript does not explicitly distinguish between exclusion due to outcomes not being measured versus exclusion due to outcome results not being reported.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country, and we also used spline regression to fit time-varying reinfection rates that did not account for heterogeneity.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies how studies were grouped for synthesis (subgroup analyses by age, variant, country, study population, and study type).

elements.quote: The exclusion criteria were: (1) The sample size was less than 20... (4) Grey literature, including a range of documents not controlled by commercial publishing organizations.
